result.summary: In 2023 Pichai mostly made broad claims about how big AI would be. The few dated predictions were short-range or medium-range: AI collaborators for professionals such as radiologists in five to ten years (60 Minutes), AI-assisted Google Docs feeling standard within a year (MIT Technology Review), and possibly more lawyers in ten years (Verge interview, seen only in Fortune's coverage). No dated or undated statement about when AGI arrives turned up, and three blog.google pages were cut off, so parts of them went unread.

reply_text:
Let me open the MIT Technology Review Q&A and the CBS 60 Minutes transcript.I found three dated AI predictions by Pichai from 2023. Neither of the two claims you've already recorded came up in a form I could reuse:

- **Magic Editor "later this year":** I did see these words in the I/O 2023 keynote post, so that file is confirmed.
- **Gemini "throughout 2024":** this appeared only in MIT Technology Review's own introduction, not in Pichai's words, so I didn't list it again.

**The three candidates:**
1. **60 Minutes (CBS, aired 16 April).** Pichai said that "five to 10 years from now" a radiologist would have an AI collaborator. CBS's transcript is an edited version of the broadcast.
2. **MIT Technology Review Q&A (published 6 December).** He said that "a year out from now" anyone opening Google Docs would expect AI help, and would find the 2022 version "so out of date."
3. **Lawyers "10 years from now."** He said he would "almost bet" there may be more lawyers in ten years. I only saw this quoted in Fortune's write-up of his 12 May interview with The Verge's Decoder podcast. I didn't open The Verge's page, so the source is marked coverage-only. This is also a forecast about AI's effect on jobs rather than about what AI will do, so it's a judgement call whether to keep it.

**Lines I left out:**
- "the next decade ahead" (MIT Technology Review): it's about society coping with AI, not AI doing something.
- AI as "the most profound in our lifetimes" (Gemini launch post): no real date.
- "Ultra … available next year" (MIT Technology Review): those are the editor's words in brackets, not his.

**Pages that were cut short:** Three blog.google pages came back truncated, so their later sections are unchecked. These were his Google-at-25 letter (cut off before its section on the future), the I/O keynote (cut off before the Gemini part) and the Gemini launch post (his note was read in full). I found no transcript of his March Hard Fork podcast or the Decoder interview, and I didn't open the November Bloomberg interview.

**Search bookkeeping:** A coding error cut the first round short after only the first fixed search had run. I then ran the other two once each, so each fixed search ran exactly once. I used all 12 searches and all 6 page openings.
